questions.question: REINFORCE multiplies the raw return G_t by the score function. What does subtracting a learned V(s_t) from G_t buy you?
options: It removes the bias a single-sample Monte Carlo return carries, so the estimator finally becomes unbiased
The estimator keeps the same expectation but its variance drops
It lets you drop the discount factor, since V(s_t) already sums the future rewards with γ folded in
It turns the on-policy update into an off-policy one
questions.explanation: A baseline that is a function of state only contributes zero in expectation, because E[∇ log π] = 0 under the policy. So the mean of the estimator is untouched and only the spread changes.

questions.question: In GAE, A_t = Σ_l (γλ)^l δ_{t+l}. What does λ = 0 collapse to?
options: A single TD residual, r_{t+1} + γV(s_{t+1}) − V(s_t)
The Monte Carlo advantage G_t − V(s_t)
An equal-weight average of every n-step advantage in the rollout
An advantage of exactly zero at every step
questions.explanation: With λ = 0 every term past l = 0 is multiplied by zero, leaving δ_t alone — the lowest-variance, most critic-biased end of the dial. λ = 1 is the opposite end and reduces to Monte Carlo.

questions.question: The entropy bonus gradient with respect to softmax logits is dH/dz_i = −p_i·(log p_i + H). Why does the distribution's own entropy H appear, rather than the constant 1 that falls out of differentiating p log p?
options: It rescales the bonus so it stays comparable across action spaces of very different sizes, keeping the coefficient c_e transferable between tasks
It guards log p_i against underflow when a probability reaches zero
Softmax normalization forces the components of any logit gradient to sum to zero, and only the −H term achieves that
It converts the entropy from nats to bits so the coefficient c_e is unitless
questions.explanation: Because softmax probabilities are constrained to sum to 1, moving all logits by the same amount changes nothing, so every valid logit gradient must sum to zero. Σ_i −p_i(log p_i + H) = H − H = 0; leaving 1 in place of H leaves a nonzero residual that shifts all logits together.

questions.question: A2C consumes each rollout for exactly one gradient step and then throws it away. What breaks if you take a second step on the same batch?
options: The critic overfits the batch and its value estimates saturate
The advantages were normalized for the first step only, so the second uses the wrong scale
The data is now off-policy for the updated π_θ, so the gradient is biased unless you add an importance-sampling correction
The entropy bonus is double-counted and the policy collapses
questions.explanation: The policy-gradient identity holds only for data drawn from the current policy. Once θ moves, the batch came from a different distribution — which is exactly the gap PPO's clipped importance ratio patches.

questions.question: After 300 updates your A2C run has policy entropy near 0.01, return stuck well below optimal, and a critic whose explained variance looks healthy. What is the first knob to turn?
options: Raise c_v above 0.5 so the critic gets a larger share of the loss budget and its targets tighten
Push λ from 0.95 toward 1.0 to remove critic bias
Add layers to the critic so it can represent V more precisely, then warm it up for a few hundred steps before re-enabling the policy gradient
Increase c_e so the entropy bonus keeps the policy stochastic
questions.explanation: Near-zero entropy with a healthy critic is entropy collapse, not a value-estimation problem: the policy stopped exploring, so no advantage signal can point it anywhere new. Raising c_e is the direct fix.

questions.question: A3C came first, yet A2C is the default in 2026. What changed?
options: A3C's lock-free gradient races were eventually shown to make its update rule mathematically incorrect on non-convex objectives
GPUs reward large batches, and A2C stacks N environments into one forward/backward pass while staying deterministic
A2C dropped the critic, so there is half as much to train
A3C needs a replay buffer, which A2C avoids
questions.explanation: A3C was designed for many cheap CPU workers; batching N synchronized envs suits GPU hardware far better and removes the nondeterminism of asynchronous updates. Neither variant uses a replay buffer, and both keep the critic.
